claims.text: The rider's threshold burden under POL-RD-08 is to show that the artifacts describe the same trip, and they do: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip id TRP-00527; the trace's first fix (2026-09-15T17:21:40+08:00) coincides with trip_record.started_at and with the recorded pickup event, and its last fix (18:56:40) coincides with trip_record.ended_at, so the pickup and completion events match across all three artifacts on the face of the record.

The excess can safely be measured from the trace itself, because the trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): it carries 571 fixes at a 10 second cadence with 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and max_gap_sec of 0.0, so there is no gap above 90 seconds, no straight-line jump above 500 m and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. The trace distance therefore governs the threshold test under POL-RD-01, and no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names is required of the rider on this record.

This trip is RYDE_POOL, so under POL-RD-12 the baseline for POL-RD-01 is the platform's matched-itinerary optimal of 58.4 km - the routing engine records it as pooled itinerary POOL-7731 matched at 17:16 with 4 riders - and not the rider's own 32.4 km solo optimal, which the clause carries as solo_optimal_distance_km for reference only. Measured on the governing trace figure of 60.91 km, the excess over the matched itinerary is 2.51 km, or 4.30% of the 58.4 km baseline. The rider states her distance position on that correct field and does not claim the 32.4 km figure as a baseline.

The rider does not overstate the position: on the correct pooled baseline the excess passes POL-RD-01's absolute limb (2.51 km is greater than 0.8 km) but fails its percentage limb (4.30% is not greater than 20% of the 58.4 km optimal), and the clause requires both tests to pass. No deviation is therefore established on this trip, and the rider does not press the POL-RD-02 recomputation - the ledger's own derived block would compute a recomputed fare of 71.36 against that route and a difference of 5.52, but POL-RD-02 runs only where POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation, and the rider will not re-characterise the trip to force it. The rider also notes that the 174 dollar bill mentioned in her claim text is not recorded on any artifact in this bundle and she does not rely on it; the amount she contests is the charged total of 76.88 on the fare ledger.

No exculpatory route is left open to the driver on this record, and the rider records that so nothing remains to be weighed against her. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00527-01, is absent: the artifact is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and the rider relies on that absence alone and not on any payload, so a POL-RD-03 exoneration cannot be run on it. The in-app chat log for this trip holds no messages at all (message_count 0), so POL-RD-04 cannot excuse any distance as rider-requested. And the driver's counterparty statement - 'Pool routes are long; that's how pool works' - cites no evidence ID, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight.

The rider has checked the pass-through and surcharge lines and finds nothing to claim under POL-RD-09: the fare carries ERP and tolls of 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, no airport surcharge on a trip that originates at NTU Hall 8 and does not originate at an airport, no cancellation fee and no waiting-time fee. The rider therefore makes no billing-integrity claim and does not ask the tribunal to construct one; she asks only that the record be measured on the fields the clauses name.

Neither profile can ground a finding about this trip. The rider's own counters are clean for the only rider-side test that exists: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so POL-RD-08's aggravated-corroboration condition (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not met and no corroboration beyond the trace may be demanded of her. On the driver's side, deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so no POL-RD-06 pattern is available in either direction. Every other field on either profile - rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld, prior_no_show_flags, prior_deviation_flags, acceptance_rate and active_region - is context only under POL-GEN-01 and cannot carry an adverse finding against the rider.

claims.text: This was a RYDE_POOL pooled trip, so the POL-RD-01 baseline is fixed by POL-RD-12 at the matched-itinerary optimal of 58.4 km recorded at match time — the trip record's optimal_route_source reads 'pooled itinerary POOL-7731 matched at 17:16; 4 riders'. The 32.4 km solo_optimal_distance_km is carried for reference only, and distance spent collecting and setting down the three co-riders on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation. Any claim that measures excess against the solo figure has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone.

Measured against the correct pooled baseline, the trace distance of 60.91 km — the figure that governs under POL-RD-01, not the rounded 60.9 km convenience copy — leaves an excess of 2.51 km, or 4.30% of the 58.4 km optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH establishment tests to pass: the excess must exceed 20% of optimal AND exceed 0.8 km absolute. The percentage test fails by an order of magnitude, 4.30% against 20%, so no deviation is established on this trip.

POL-RD-01 is explicit on the consequence: if either establishment test fails, no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, save only for a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4). The rider's characterisation — that she was 'charged for everybody's trip' — does not conjure a deviation the numbers do not show. The present state of the ledger should stand: payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02's optimal-route recomputation is never reached and no refund of any part of the contested 76.88 has an arithmetic basis. I do not ask the tribunal to run a recomputation to which the threshold failure has denied it a licence.

The GPS trace is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0: 571 fixes at a 10 s sample interval, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0 and an empty gaps list. It meets none of the impairment limbs of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) — no gap over 90 s, no 500 m jump, no sustained interval above 30 s — so the 'no deviation' measurement is reliable, needs no independent corroboration, and cannot drag the case toward a POL-RD-10(3) escalation.

The ledger charges exactly the metered rate card for the distance and time actually driven: base 3.80 + 0.75 x 60.9 km (45.68) + 0.28 x 95.0 min (26.60) + 0.80 platform fee = 76.88, with zero ERP, zero tolls, zero airport surcharge, zero waiting-time fee, zero promo and surge_multiplier 1.0. The rider's reference to a '174 dollar' bill finds no support anywhere in the fare_breakdown, and there is no charge line without a counterpart to trigger a POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity correction.

The driver's counter-statement — 'Pool routes are long; that's how pool works. The app splits the fare, not me' — is consistent with the record: the matched itinerary was 58.4 km against a 32.4 km solo route, and the fare is computed and split by the platform, not by the driver. The rider's dissatisfaction with the length of a pooled route is a complaint about the product she chose 'to save money', not evidence that the driver deviated, and the policy provides no distance refund for it.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden: she must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace, and only then must the driver invoke a specific exculpatory clause. She has not cleared even the first stage — the record shows a 4.30% excess against a 20% gate — so the burden never shifts and no exculpatory clause need be reached.

The bundle also holds a MISSING traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00527-01, admissibility status MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload — I disclose that impairment expressly. The driver asserts no external traffic cause at all (his explanation is that pool routes are simply long), so no exculpatory clause is invoked against this or any missing artifact; under POL-RD-13 an uncited traffic excuse is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, and here there is neither an excuse nor a citation. The absence is immaterial to the outcome.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this was a RYDE_POOL trip (TRP-00527). POL-RD-12 fixes the route-deviation baseline for a pooled trip at the platform's matched-itinerary optimal of 58.4 km recorded at match time (routing engine: pooled itinerary POOL-7731, 4 riders), not the 32.4 km solo figure, which the record carries only as solo_optimal_distance_km for reference. Measured on the governing trace figure of 60.91 km (EV-GPS-00527), the excess over that baseline is 2.51 km, or 4.30% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH establishment tests to pass — more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute. The absolute limb passes, but the percentage limb fails by a wide margin, so no deviation is established and, under POL-RD-01, the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. POL-RD-02's optimal-route recomputation is therefore never reached and no part of the contested 76.88 has an arithmetic basis. The present state of the ledger stands: payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

The rider's concern that she was 'charged for everybody's trip' is answered by POL-RD-12: a pooled route is longer by construction, the co-riders' collection and set-down legs are part of the matched itinerary and are excluded from excess precisely by using that baseline, and the policy provides no distance refund for the length of a pooled route the rider chose. The '174 dollar' figure in the claim finds no support on any artifact — the fare ledger's charged_total is 76.88, computed as base 3.80 + 0.75 x 60.9 km (45.68) + 0.28 x 95.0 min (26.60) + 0.80 platform fee, with zero ERP, zero tolls, zero airport surcharge, zero waiting-time fee, zero promo and surge_multiplier 1.0 (read from the fare_breakdown).

The driver's counter-statement ('Pool routes are long; that's how pool works. The app splits the fare, not me') cites no evidence ID and so carries no weight under POL-RD-08; it is not needed, because the rider's own threshold showing fails. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00527-01 (status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload) is immaterial: no party asserted an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 was never invoked, the comparison cannot be run, and its absence is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) escalation.

No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires. The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) — 571 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, empty gaps list, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and no POL-RD-07(ii) corroboration is required. Trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, pickup and completion timestamps agree, and no charge line lacks a counterpart, so POL-RD-10(2), (4) and (8) do not apply. No billing-integrity correction arises under POL-RD-09: there are no ERP or toll lines, no airport surcharge on a trip originating at NTU Hall 8, and no phantom gantry, so no POL-RD-09(4) referral is produced. No POL-RD-06 pattern exists (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 250), and the rider's counters (deviation_claims_60d 0, substantiated 0) impose no aggravated-corroboration condition under POL-RD-08. No profile field outside those POL-GEN-01 names for those tests was used as a ground.

Confidence is 0.9, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts (EV-GPS-00527 and EV-TRIP-00527) that carry the deciding measurement.

To the rider and the driver: the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence, and the fare of SGD 76.88 stands unchanged.

Distance spent collecting and setting down the other passengers on a matched pooled itinerary is not a deviation. The '32 km' comparison uses the wrong field, which the trip record carries as solo_optimal_distance_km for reference only.

The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00527) records 60.91 km actually driven; the trip record's rounded 60.9 km is a convenience copy and under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs. Measured against the correct 58.4 km baseline, the excess is 2.51 km, or 4.30%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed 20% of the optimal AND exceed 0.8 km in absolute terms; both tests must pass and the percentage test does not come close. No deviation is established, so POL-RD-02's optimal-route recomputation is never reached and no part of the SGD 76.88 is refundable. The SGD 174 figure in the claim text appears on no artifact in the bundle; the amount charged and contested is SGD 76.88.

The trace is complete — 571 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so it meets none of the impairment limbs of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and no corroboration question arises. The fare ledger reads base 3.80 + distance 45.68 + time 26.60 + platform fee 0.80 = 76.88, with ERP and tolls 0.00, no airport surcharge or waiting fee, no promo, and a surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown. Every line has a counterpart in the trace and trip record, so there is no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) and no referral is produced.

To the driver: the statement that pool routes are simply long is consistent with the record, but the case is decided on the instruments, not on that statement, which carries no weight multiplier. No traffic cause was asserted against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and, per POL-RD-13, the absent advisory EV-ADVIS-00527-01 (status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. No POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation pattern arises: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, and the trip shows no material deviation in any event.

Both profiles were cited only to confirm that neither profile test is met (rider deviation_claims_60d 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0, so no aggravated corroboration applies; driver deviation_flags_90d 0). The remaining profile fields — rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld, prior_no_show_flags, prior_deviation_flags, acceptance_rate and active_region — are context only under POL-GEN-01, and no adverse finding rests on them.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The charge of SGD 76.88 remains as recorded; payment_status stays CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd stays 0.00. Confidence 0.90, capped at 1.0 by the weight of the instruments carrying the deciding facts (GPS trace, trip record and fare breakdown, each at weight 1.0).

The governing trace figure (EV-GPS-00527, weight 1.0) is 60.91 km, so the excess is 2.51 km, or 4.30% of 58.4 km. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of the optimal (11.68 km) and 0.8 km absolute; the 2.51 km clears the absolute limb but fails the 20% limb, so no deviation is established and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. Because POL-RD-01 establishes no deviation, POL-RD-02's recomputation is never reached and no distance-or-time refund has any arithmetic basis: the ledger's payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 stand.

The rider's account of being billed for the other passengers is the product she chose: on a matched pooled itinerary the route is longer than her solo trip by design, and POL-RD-12 excludes co-rider collection and set-down distance from any excess. The '174 dollar' figure in her filing does not appear on any artifact in this bundle. The amount actually charged, and the amount contested, is 76.88, which the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00527) builds from the metered rate card: 3.80 base + 45.68 distance (0.75 x 60.9 km) + 26.60 time (0.28 x 95.0 min) + 0.80 platform fee, with zero ERP, zero tolls, no airport surcharge, no waiting fee, no promo and surge 1.0. There is accordingly no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09: no gantry line (empty erp_gantries) and no airport surcharge on a trip originating at NTU Hall 8, so nothing is refundable on that footing.

The driver's counter-statement is consistent with the record, but as an assertion citing no evidence ID it carries no independent weight under POL-RD-08; the outcome does not turn on it. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00527-01 (status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) was disclosed by both sides; no party invokes POL-RD-03, so its absence changes nothing and, under POL-RD-13, an advisory nobody cites for an external-cause excuse is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c): 571 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so no independent corroboration is required. No profile field grounds any finding (POL-GEN-01): driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips, so no POL-RD-06 pattern exists and no conduct referral follows, and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no aggravated corroboration applies. Confidence is 0.95: the deciding facts rest on EV-GPS-00527 and EV-TRIP-00527, both at weight_multiplier 1.0. No clause produces a referral, so the referrals list is empty. Nothing moves: the charge stands.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: the contested charge of SGD 76.88 stands, and no refund or compensation is due. This was a RYDE_POOL trip, so under POL-RD-12 the measuring baseline is the platform's matched-itinerary optimal of 58.4 km (EV-TRIP-00527.optimal_distance_km; the routing engine records 'pooled itinerary POOL-7731 matched at 17:16; 4 riders'), NOT the 32.4 km solo_optimal_distance_km the rider has in mind — POL-RD-12 carries that solo figure for reference only, and a claim measured against it fails on that ground alone. The governing distance is the trace figure of 60.91 km (EV-GPS-00527.trace_distance_km, which governs over the rounded 60.9 km convenience copy on the trip record under POL-RD-01). Excess = 60.91 − 58.4 = 2.51 km, i.e. 4.30% of the matched-itinerary optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH establishment tests to pass: the absolute limb passes (2.51 km > 0.8 km) but the percentage limb fails (4.30% is not greater than 20%). No deviation is therefore established, POL-RD-02's recomputation is never reached, and there is no arithmetic basis for any refund of the 76.88. On the rider's 'charged for everybody's trip' theory: POL-RD-12 provides that distance spent collecting and setting down co-riders on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation, and the 58.4 km matched-itinerary baseline already comprehends that distance — the rider's own advocate accepted this and did not press the POL-RD-02 recomputation. On the '174 dollar' bill in the claim text: no artifact in the bundle records it. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00527) shows a charged total of 76.88, made up of base fare 3.80 + distance 0.75 × 60.9 km = 45.68 + time 0.28 × 95.0 min = 26.60 + platform fee 0.80, with ERP/tolls 0.00, no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee, no promo, and surge_multiplier 1.0 read from the fare breakdown; the rider states she does not rely on the 174 figure. On billing integrity (POL-RD-09(4)): there are no ERP gantries, no tolls, no airport surcharge on a trip originating at NTU Hall 8, and no charge line without a counterpart, so nothing is refundable as a standalone correction. On trace integrity: EV-GPS-00527 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 571 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and max_gap_sec 0.0, so it meets none of the POL-RD-07(a)–(c) impairment limbs; the finding that no deviation exists rests on that trace (weight 1.0) and the trip record (weight 1.0), and confidence is above the 0.70 floor. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00527-01 (status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) is disclosed, but neither party asserts an external traffic cause — the driver's statement is that pool routes are simply long — so no exculpatory clause is invoked against it, the absence decides nothing, and it does not trigger POL-RD-10(5) or a POL-RD-13 escalation. The driver's counterparty statement that 'pool routes are long; that's how pool works. The app splits the fare, not me' is consistent with the record, but I have not needed to rely on it; the outcome turns on the measured figures. On the profiles: only the fields POL-GEN-01 makes citable were consulted — rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 (so POL-RD-08's aggravated-corroboration condition is not met), and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250 (so no POL-RD-06 pattern arises); every other profile field is context only and none was used to establish any fact about this trip.
